steps.title: Connect power in and Ground
steps.note: Mount the rail, the StamPLC and the Wago connectors, then connect power in and Ground. Connectors: DC jack J1: + red, − black; inline fuse holder FU1: lead 1 red, lead 2 red; power button Q1: IN red, GND black. Press an M3 heat-set insert into each of the two rail pads in the base (soldering iron, straight down, flush with the pad) and screw the rail on from above with an M3×6 pan-head screw and a washer. Clip the StamPLC on the rail, front towards the lid. Clip the Wagos into the rack on the front wall, wire entries up, levers towards the unit, left to right: X-24, X-0V1, X-0V2, X-S, X-V. Put a ferrule on every wire end that goes under a screw. Pass each cable that leaves the box through the oval exit before you strip it. Unplug the supply and disconnect the air. J1: wire 1 on the centre-pin lug (+); with three lugs, wire 3 on the one that stays connected to the sleeve with the plug in (meter). Solder lugs: solder and heat-shrink. FU1 sits in the lead from J1 to Q1; the fuse goes in last. Wire 5 joins the two Ground Wagos. Every slot of a Wago is connected to all the others: use one wire per slot. Check with a meter: the centre pin of the plug is +24 V.

connections.la: DC jack J1 + (+24 V, centre pin)

steps.title: Connect the StamPLC
steps.note: Connect the power button Q1 to the +24 V Wago X-24, then the StamPLC to X-24 and to Ground. Connectors: power button Q1: OUT red; StamPLC: + red, − black, C black. Q1 is the lit POWER rocker. IN and OUT are the two connectors that connect when it is switched on, GND is the third (wire 6 on GND shorts the supply). Flat tabs: insulated receptacles. Wire 4 gives the Q1 lamp its Ground. Terminal C of the StamPLC is the common of all eight inputs: it goes to Ground (wire 9), which suits PNP sensors. Check: POWER off, the Q1 lamp stays dark (lit: swap wires 2 and 6). Then insert the fuse, POWER on: the StamPLC starts and shows its screen. POWER off.

connections.lb: Wago X-24 (+24 V after POWER) slot 1

connections.la: Wago X-24 (+24 V after POWER) slot 2

steps.title: Connect E-STOP and the pressure switch
steps.note: Connect X-24 through the E-STOP and the pressure switch to the valve rail, and report both rails to the StamPLC. Connectors: E-STOP button: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red; pressure switch QPM11: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red; StamPLC: input 3 red, input 4 red. The valve rail X-V is live only while POWER is on, E-STOP is released and the air pressure is below the trip. E-STOP uses its closed contact: terminals 1 and 2, marked 11 and 12 on the contact block. Pressure switch QPM11: both cores of its cable are on the +24 V side (red) and it has no polarity; with no air, a meter must beep across its two terminals (closed contact type). The StamPLC inputs 3 and 4 only read the two rails: input 3 on shows E-STOP released, input 4 on shows the pressure is fine. An input accepts either polarity, it only needs the voltage between the input and C. E-STOP and the pressure switch cut only the valve rail: the StamPLC stays powered and shows the fault. Check: POWER on, air off: inputs 3 and 4 on; press E-STOP: both off.

steps.title: Connect the end sensors
steps.note: Connect the two end sensors. Connectors: StamPLC: input 1 black, input 2 black. Keep each sensor's own wire colours: brown wire = +24 V from X-24, blue wire = Ground, black wire = signal. These are PNP sensors: check the label SMT-8M-A-PS-… (PS = PNP). B0 reports home on input 1, B1 reports front on input 2. The signal wire drives the StamPLC input directly. If an input reads on with its sensor off (leakage current of the sensor), add a 4.7 kΩ resistor from that input to C. Position: B0 so input 1 is on with the rod fully home, B1 so input 2 is on 2–3 mm before the press bottoms.

steps.title: Connect the valve coils
steps.note: Connect the two valve coils through their plugs and relays 1 and 2 of the StamPLC. Connectors: valve plug Y1: pin 1 red, pin 2 black; valve plug Y2: pin 1 red, pin 2 black; StamPLC: relay 1 NC red, relay 1 COM red, relay 1 NO red, relay 2 COM red, relay 2 NO red. Y1 extends; Y2 retracts. Pin 1 is +24 V (red): mark that core at both ends of each valve cable. Relay terminals are NC, COM and NO: follow the labels on the unit, they are not in the order of this drawing. Relay 1 COM comes from the valve rail X-V, relay 1 NC feeds relay 2 COM, so relay 1 and 2 can never switch the two coils on together. Inside each plug, fit D7/D8 with the cores: ring on pin 1 (+), plain leg on pin 2; reversed, they short the supply. Leave them out only if the plug's datasheet shows built-in suppression (an LED alone is not enough). The plugs fit either coil: with air on, press the red manual button next to each coil; the coil that drives the rod out gets plug Y1. Check without air, meter on the plug pins, with the bench program (firmware/bench) toggling the relays: both off, neither plug is live; relay 1 on, only Y1 is live; relay 2 on, only Y2 is live; both on, only Y1 is live.

steps.title: Rail, relays and diodes
steps.note: Mount the rail, the relay sockets and the Wago connectors, then fit a diode on each relay socket. Press an M3 heat-set insert into each of the three rail pads in the base (soldering iron, straight down, flush with the pad), then screw the rail on from above with an M3×6 pan-head screw and a washer, through the slots 37.5, 137.5 and 187.5 mm from the K1 end of the rail. Clip the sockets on the rail with their 1/4 end towards the back wall, so the busy 13/14 end faces the console. Clip the Wagos into the rack on the back wall, wire entries up, levers towards the relays: X-EN, X-M1, X-M2, X-D. Diodes D1–D4: ring to 14, plain leg to 13; crimp each leg into a 0.5 mm² ferrule. Put a ferrule on every wire end that goes under a screw. Pass each cable that leaves the box through its gland before you strip it.

steps.title: Connect power in and Ground
steps.note: Connect the power jack J1 to the fuse F1 (red) and J1 to Ground (black), then take Ground to both Ground blocks and to the coil of every relay. Connectors: DC jack J1: + red, − black; fuse holder F1: tab 1 red. Crimp wires 6 and 7a into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K1 terminal 13. Crimp wires 7a and 7b into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K2 terminal 13. Crimp wires 7b and 7c into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K3 terminal 13. Unplug the supply and disconnect the air. J1: wire 1 on the centre-pin lug (+); with three lugs, wire 4 on the one that stays connected to the sleeve with the plug in (meter). Solder lugs: solder and heat-shrink; flat tabs: insulated receptacles. On terminal 13 of each relay the diode leg from step A goes on the other side of the screw, in its own ferrule. Every slot of a Wago is connected to all the others: use one wire per slot. Check with a meter: the centre pin of the plug is +24 V.

steps.note: Connect the relays to each other. Crimp wires 26 and 27 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K3 terminal 5. steps.title: Connect the power button and E-STOP
steps.note: Connect the fuse F1 to the power button Q1 (the blue one on the board), then the power button to E-STOP and to Ground. Connectors: fuse holder F1: tab 2 red; power button Q1: IN red, OUT red, GND black; E-STOP button: terminal 1 red. Q1 is the lit POWER button. IN and OUT are the two connectors that connect when it is switched on, GND is the third (wire 3 on GND shorts the supply). Flat tabs: insulated receptacles. E-STOP uses its closed contact: terminals 1 and 2, marked 11 and 12 on the contact block. E-STOP and the pressure switch feed X-EN directly, so E-STOP cuts all control power. Wire 15 gives the Q1 lamp its Ground. Check: POWER off, the Q1 lamp stays dark (lit: swap wires 2 and 3). Then each relay: plug it in, POWER on, test lead from E-STOP terminal 1 to its terminal 14: it clicks and its LED lights. POWER off, relays out again until the wiring is done.

steps.title: Connect STOP, START and JOG
steps.note: Connect STOP, START and JOG to the relays and the timer. Connectors: STOP button: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red; START button: terminal 3 red and red, terminal 4 red; JOG button: terminal 3 red, terminal 4 red and red. Crimp wires 11 and 12 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K1 terminal 9. Crimp wires 12 and 20 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at START button terminal 3 (open contact, marked 23). Crimp wires 13 and 14 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K1 terminal 5. Crimp wires 21 and 22 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at JOG button terminal 4 (open contact, marked 24). Crimp wires 21 and 23 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K3 terminal 9. Crimp wires 22 and 24 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K1 terminal 8. STOP uses its closed contact: terminals 1 and 2, marked 11 and 12 on the contact block. START and JOG use their open contact: terminals 3 and 4, marked 23 and 24. If your block is marked 21 and 22 or 13 and 14, go by the contact type. A meter beeps across a closed contact until the button is pressed and across an open contact only while it is pressed. Wire 10 takes the timer contact (T1 pins 8 and 5) to STOP: that contact, STOP and START with the K1 holding contact form the AUTO latch. Wire 20 feeds JOG from START's input, after STOP and the timer contact, so STOP and a jam stop JOG too. K1 (AUTO, wire 22) and JOG feed the same point, so the press runs while K1 is on or while JOG is held. After power-on and after STOP, E-STOP, a jam or an air pressure fault, K1 is off and the press moves only while you hold JOG; START resumes automatic mode. The K1 LED shows it.

steps.title: Connect the valve coils
steps.note: Connect the two valve coils through their plugs, and the timer diodes D5 and D6 to the same relay terminals. Connectors: valve plug Y1: pin 1 red, pin 2 black; valve plug Y2: pin 1 red, pin 2 black. Crimp wires 33 and 37 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K2 terminal 1. Crimp wires 35 and 38 into one twin ferrule, then one screw at Relay K3 terminal 8. Y1 extends; Y2 retracts. Pin 1 is +24 V (red): mark that core at both ends of each valve cable. Inside each plug, fit D7/D8 with the cores: ring on pin 1 (+), plain leg on pin 2; reversed, they short the supply. Leave them out only if the plug's datasheet shows built-in suppression (an LED alone is not enough). D5's plain leg joins wire 37 in one 2-way Wago (221-412), D6's joins wire 38 in another (never 37 with 38: that ties Y1 to Y2); sleeve the bare legs with heat-shrink. The plugs fit either coil: with air on, press the red manual button next to each coil; the coil that drives the rod out gets plug Y1. K3 interlocks the coils: they can never be on together.

steps.title: Connect the jam timer
steps.note: Connect the jam timer T1 (the 8-pin timer) and the diode legs that feed it. Jam timer T1 ends automatic mode when a stroke takes too long. The numbers 1 to 8 are the pin numbers printed on the timer base. The timer must run on 24 V DC (+24 V on pin 7, Ground on pin 2), start counting when it gets power, restart from zero while its reset input (pins 1 and 3) is closed, and have one changeover contact (this build uses pins 8 and 5). T1 runs only while a valve coil is on and the rod is away from home: K4 closes the reset at home and holds the time at zero. Bend each ring leg of D5 and D6 straight into its X-D slot, no wire. Set the wheels with no coil on (the timer reads them at power-up): left wheel (T1, relay off) about twice one out-and-back, 30 s until you have timed it; right wheel (T2, relay on) 1 s, never 0. Test without air: rod a few cm off home, press START: after T1 the timer clicks and K1 drops. A jam stops JOG too; let go before you try again. If your timer is different: match the supply (24 V DC), a reset input and one changeover contact, and map the pins of your base onto the pins named here. A contact block (marks like 11 and 12, or 23 and 24, as behind the buttons) is not a timer and cannot replace it.

connections.la: Wago X-EN (+24 V while on) slot 3

steps.title: Connect the pressure switch and the end sensors
steps.note: Connect E-STOP to the pressure switch and on to X-EN, then the two end sensors. Connectors: E-STOP button: terminal 2 red; pressure switch QPM11: terminal 1 red, terminal 2 red. X-EN is the control +24 V: live while POWER is on, E-STOP is released and the air pressure is below the trip. Pressure switch QPM11: both cores of its cable are on the +24 V side (red) and it has no polarity; with no air, a meter must beep across its two terminals (closed contact type). Keep each sensor's own wire colours: brown wire = +24 V from X-EN, blue wire = Ground, black wire = signal. These are PNP sensors: check the label SMT-8M-A-PS-… (PS = PNP). B1 drives K2 (front); B0 drives K4 (home). The signal wire (max 100 mA) drives the relay coil (37 mA) directly. Position: B0 so K4 lights with the rod fully home, B1 so K2 lights 2–3 mm before the press bottoms.

steps.title: Supply → filter-regulator
steps.note: Mount the FRL upright on its bracket at the board edge, bowls hanging vertically and drains pointing down off the board, away from the control box. Follow the arrow on the FRL body. Supply: 7–10 bar; start with the regulator at 2 bar. If the unit has a lubricator, leave it empty: the cylinder and the valve are greased for life, and once you oil them you have to keep oiling. Check: Hose retained; FRL flow arrow points towards the valve.

steps.title: Filter-regulator → shut-off
steps.note: Fit the 3/2 shut-off with exhaust right after the FRL, its arrow pointing away from the FRL. Closed, it cuts the supply and vents everything after it: tee, pressure switch, valve and cylinder. Close it whenever you reach into the press. Check: Arrow points away from the FRL; exhaust port open, not plugged.

steps.title: Shut-off → pressure-switch tee
steps.note: Connect the shut-off outlet to the 6 mm tee. The QPM11 sits on the tee's branch and measures the regulated supply pressure. Set it to open at 6 bar: regulator at 6 bar (only for this setting), POWER on, rod pushed home by hand so the K4 LED lights, turn its screw until K4 goes out; then back to 5.5 bar or less. Check: Pressure switch after the shut-off; tee branch sealed.

steps.title: Tee → valve supply
steps.note: Connect the tee to P, the supply port. Read the letters on the valve body: never connect the supply to R or S (the exhausts). Check: Tube reaches P; no tight bend or kink.

steps.title: Valve A → cylinder cap end
steps.note: Connect A to the end without the rod. Fit a meter-out flow control: free flow into the cylinder, restricted flow out. This cap-end adjuster controls retraction speed. Start with both flow controls 1 turn open. Check: A reaches the cap end; flow-control direction confirmed.

steps.title: Valve B → cylinder rod end
steps.note: Connect B to the port beside the rod. Again use meter-out orientation. This rod-end adjuster controls extension speed. Leave room for cylinder movement. Check: B reaches the rod end; tube cannot rub or pull tight.

steps.title: Fit both exhaust silencers
steps.note: Fit one silencer to each exhaust and point both away from the control box and the operator. Do not cap or join these ports to supply. First air-on, POWER off: nothing may move and the lever must stay free by hand. If the rod creeps out, the valve is not exhaust-centre: close the shut-off. Check: Both exhausts open through silencers; no obstruction.
